A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEA-Bench research. Their main text, Appendices A–G, figures, tables, and equations are readable and can be matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LLMs, fine-tuning experiments, and human validation results (Tables 1–2 and 7–8).

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, fine-tuning outcomes, and human validation results (Tables 1–2 and 7–8).

M1.justification: Scenario construction, the 31-tool MCP environment, hallucination detection, user simulation, and LoRA fine-tuning remain unchanged. The operational prompts in Appendix G also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use 81 ExTES-derived scenarios, action-oriented and emotion-oriented users, and the same 365-dialogue TEA-Dialog dataset. The seen/unseen scenario evaluation is retained; no memory task is added.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 5, and 6 retain the same nine models in tool/no-tool comparisons. Table 2 retains the same Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B base/fine-tuned comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain the 15-turn cap, scoring metrics, training on the first 60 scenarios with evaluation on all 81, and the 150-dialogue/150-response human evaluation samples. Training budgets and model configurations also match.

E4.justification: The user-type comparisons, tool-use and hallucination analyses, dialogue-stage analyses, human validation, and fine-tuning generalization analysis are retained. Appendix relocations introduce no new analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same correlation and agreement reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–2 and 5–9 and Figures 5–12 match. For example, GPT-4o-mini's with-tool TEA score remains 81.11, and the fine-tuned Qwen3-8B ID/OOD TEA scores remain 79.92/74.52.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 retains the same factuality and hallucination definitions and macro-averaging equations (1)–(6). No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark novelty claim, capacity-dependent benefits of tool use, and limited fine-tuning generalization. The TEA-Bench and TEA-Dialog contributions are unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 already acknowledges limited interaction horizons. v2 adds a specific Long-term Memory limitation identifying conversational memory recall and retention as unevaluated. Other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page repository URL for code and data, absent in v1. Training, hardware, and prompt details in Appendices F–G are unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CAUAIN and TransESC citations and a joint emotion–semantic modeling mention. The new memory limitation cites four additional works. This modestly expands research context without redefining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized related-work edits, adds a limitation paragraph and acknowledgments, and fixes a duplicated comma. The scientific narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays retain their content and design but are repositioned: Figure 6 changes columns on PDF page 7, and Tables 3–4 move one page later. v2 also removes printed page-number footers.

improvement.justification: The new code/data pointer and explicit memory limitation modestly improve access guidance and scope clarity over v1. Methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged. Removing printed page numbers slightly weakens navigation, but does not outweigh these limited documentation gains.
